96: ✦Your baby is making sucking movements and may even be able to put a thumb in their mouth.✦Now that the eyes and ears are in the right place on the head, your baby looks more and more 'human'.
97: ✦You may start getting varicose veins.✦They can be painful.✦Avoiding standing for long periods and stretching your legs now and then can help prevent them.✦Compression stockings can also help.
98: ✦You may have some vaginal discharge this week.✦If it's white, don't worry.✦If it's yellowish and smells bad, tell your doctor.
99: ✦Your doctor may suggest an amniocentesis around this stage.✦While in the amniotic fluid, the baby sheds some skin cells into it.✦Amniocentesis examines these cells to determine the chromosomes. Since reliable information can be obtained by now, doctors usually suggest it at 15–16 weeks.✦But it can be done up to weeks 18–26.
100: ✦Indigestion, heartburn, tiredness, constipation, increased appetite, a stuffy nose, nosebleeds, bleeding gums, headaches, swollen feet and ankles and varicose veins.✦Similar to PMS, you may have mood swings, cry easily, get suddenly angry or have irrational thoughts.
101: ✦If your pregnancy is normal, stay active during the day.✦If your body is active during the day, you'll sleep much better.✦Don't take very long naps during the day.✦Try to go to bed at the same time every night.✦Low blood sugar can keep you awake.✦A light snack like yogurt before bed helps.✦Avoid heavy food before sleeping; it can keep you awake.
102: ✦You can sleep on your back until your belly gets heavy, at around 4–5 months.✦But it's a good idea to start getting used to sleeping on your left side from now.✦Lying on your back can make back pain worse as your belly gets heavier. It can also bring stomach problems. Lying on your back also puts pressure under the uterus, on the vessels that carry blood back to the heart. Too little blood reaching the heart is risky for mother and baby. That's why lying on your side is better.
103: ✦Many babies lie turned to the left in the womb.✦This prevents pressure on the large vein on the right side of your body.✦Lying on your left side keeps your circulation healthy.✦It also helps your baby's circulation.✦And you'll sleep more comfortably.
104: ✦You'll notice your nose runs more, you produce more saliva and you sweat more.✦That's because there's more fluid in your body.✦Nosebleeds are common because the tiny vessels in the nose widen.
105: ✦Take a good look at your teeth in the mirror.✦You may notice red, tender, swollen gums that bleed when you brush.✦Pregnancy hormones make your gums react differently to plaque, causing gum inflammation (gingivitis).✦It's usually harmless and painless.✦It usually goes away on its own, but if you don't care for your teeth, gingivitis can progress to infection of the jawbone and tissues.✦Prevention is key: good oral hygiene – brushing at least twice a day and flossing – will reduce gum recession, bleeding and sensitivity.
106: ✦Pregnancy hormones may make your eyes dry and itchy.✦If you wear contact lenses, you may want to switch to glasses.✦You can also use eye drops recommended by your doctor.
107: ✦Many women experience cravings during pregnancy.✦They can be very specific – like wanting peaches only at a certain ripeness.✦Or more general, like wanting spicy food.✦As long as you crave healthy things, you can eat as much as you like without worry.✦But make sure your diet stays varied beyond what you crave.✦Eating nutritious food now will affect your baby's development and future health.
108: ✦Some women experience a type of craving called pica.✦Pica is an appetite for non-food substances like plaster, paint chips, clay, coal, chalk and laundry detergent. It's thought to be linked to mineral deficiency, but the craved substance doesn't necessarily fix it. If you have unusual cravings like this, talk to your doctor.
109: ✦Start the day with a nutritious breakfast.✦Include enough protein, carbohydrates, fibre and some healthy fats. Choose vegetables, whole grains, lean meat and low-fat dairy.✦Avoid processed foods, junk food and very sugary desserts.
110: ✦Have a milkshake with some fresh fruit every day.✦You'll get plenty of calories plus the calcium from the ice cream.✦Eat foods with good fats.✦Like nuts and avocado.
111: ✦Eat dried fruit.✦Since it isn't as filling as fresh fruit, you'll eat more.✦That way you get more healthy calories.✦Snack often between meals.✦Remind yourself that you need to gain weight for both you and your baby.
112: ✦Time to enjoy your pregnancy! The uncomfortable symptoms of early pregnancy have probably gone and you have more energy.✦Enjoy this time by staying active – walking, swimming or joining a yoga class.✦Now that your bump is showing, treat yourself to maternity clothes that flatter your new shape.
113: ✦You may have started to feel off-balance.✦As your belly grows, your centre of gravity shifts.✦That can make you feel unsteady on your feet at times.✦Avoid situations where you might fall. Wear flat shoes.
114: ✦Injuries can be dangerous for you and your baby.✦Always wear your seatbelt in the car.✦Keep the lap belt below your bump and the shoulder belt between your breasts.
115: ✦You may still have dry eyes.✦Eye drops recommended by your doctor will help.✦Your contact lenses may bother you.✦Switching to glasses will make you more comfortable.
116: ✦You keep gaining weight.✦This may worry you at first.✦But focus on eating well.✦Your skin may change.✦It will stretch, especially over your breasts and belly, as your body prepares.✦This can cause itching.✦Special creams can help.✦They may even help prevent stretch marks.
117: ✦Later in pregnancy, darkened or brown spots or small red spots may appear on your face.✦These come from widened tiny blood vessels and usually disappear after birth.
118: ✦Vitamin D is important for a healthy pregnancy diet.✦It balances your calcium and phosphate levels and supports your baby's bone development.✦If you're deficient, your baby's bones may not get strong enough.✦In some cases it can even cause serious problems.
119: ✦This week your baby's mammary glands and nipples are forming.✦In baby girls, millions of eggs keep forming in the ovaries.✦By birth this number will drop to about one to two million.✦In baby boys, the prostate will start forming next week.✦The eyes are moving into place and moving around, but the baby can't open the eyelids yet.
120: ✦If this is your first pregnancy, you may soon feel your baby moving.✦This fluttering is known as 'quickening'. As your baby grows, you'll feel stronger movements and, in the coming weeks, even kicks.✦But every mother is different, so you may feel it earlier (common if this isn't your first baby) or later.✦So if you haven't felt anything by 18 weeks, don't worry.
121: ✦At this stage your body is going through many circulatory changes, such as increased blood volume and rapidly widening blood vessels, which can lower blood pressure.✦This can make you dizzy if not enough blood reaches your upper body and head.
122: ✦This week you may notice your feet getting bigger.✦This is partly due to water retention, known as oedema, seen in the second trimester and later.✦Hormones are another reason.✦Relaxin, the pregnancy hormone that loosens your pelvic muscles so your baby can settle into the birth canal, also loosens the ligaments in your feet, so the bones spread.✦Keeping your feet up and a cool foot bath can ease swollen feet.✦Don't worry (and enjoy it!) – it's your excuse to go shoe shopping.
123: ✦Sudden dizziness.✦Your heart is working 40–50% harder than before pregnancy.✦Combined with the pressure of your growing uterus on blood vessels, this can cause occasional dizziness, especially when you stand up quickly.✦Rest often.✦Lie on your side when you feel dizzy.✦Low blood sugar can also make you light-headed.✦Resting, lying on your side or eating a piece of fruit will raise your blood sugar and ease the dizziness.
124: ✦Tiny movements.✦Most women start noticing their baby's movements between weeks 16 and 20.✦Since your baby is still very small, this week you may feel gentle flutters rather than strong kicks.
125: ✦Leg cramps.✦This week you may get leg cramps, usually at night.✦Try stretching your calf muscles before bed and drink plenty of water. A warm bath, hot shower or massage can also help.
126: ✦Nose problems.✦Due to increased hormones and blood volume swelling the mucous membranes, you may have nosebleeds and a stuffy nose.✦Lower back pain.✦Your growing belly and hormonal changes can cause pain in your lower back.
127: ✦You may feel tired and low on energy.✦This common symptom is mostly due to hormonal changes and your heart working harder.✦Your circulatory system is going through big changes, and it's normal for your blood pressure to be lower than usual during this period.
128: ✦If you haven't had it yet, your doctor may suggest the triple or quadruple screening test, recommended between weeks 16 and 20.✦These may not be needed if no risk was found in the first-trimester screening.✦Even with normal early results, factors like the mother's age or a family history of genetic conditions may make these tests advisable.✦Along with the scan, the baby's main organs, body systems, head and spine, brain, placenta position, amniotic fluid volume, heartbeat, blood vessels and sex are checked.✦The quadruple test is more comprehensive than the triple test.✦Doctors today usually prefer the quadruple test for that reason.✦If these tests show a risk, the doctor may suggest amniocentesis or other tests.
129: ✦Your blood volume keeps increasing.✦Your heart pumps almost 7 litres of blood a minute.✦Even so, your heart rate doesn't rise much.✦Your blood pressure isn't affected because your blood vessels have widened since early pregnancy.✦Progesterone and other pregnancy hormones play a big role in this widening.✦Of course, this protective state won't keep your blood pressure normal forever.✦After about this week, your blood pressure may rise slightly.✦What's normal is that it doesn't rise quickly or excessively.
130: ✦At 19 weeks, as your belly grows, your centre of gravity shifts. Be very careful about falls and slips. In winter, avoid going out on snowy or icy days. Always go up and down stairs slowly and calmly. – Your posture may change as your belly grows. Try not to slouch. Walking with your shoulders back will reduce back pain.
131: ✦Drink plenty of water to avoid urinary tract infections.✦Wash your hands before using the toilet.✦Your appetite may increase a lot this week.✦Avoid overeating. As your belly grows, stretch marks may appear.✦To help prevent them, you can apply almond oil, cocoa butter or coconut oil to your skin a few times a day.✦You can also mix these oils and apply the blend. To keep pregnancy skin patches from darkening, avoid too much sun.
132: ✦During pregnancy you may hear unwanted advice or superstitious ways to guess the baby's sex.✦Some of this advice isn't scientific.✦Don't believe everything you hear; note what confuses you and ask your doctor.✦You may even get unexpected comments from strangers you pass on the street.✦Don't take them too seriously.✦Instead of getting angry, try to see the funny side.
133: ✦You may notice redness on your palms.✦This is due to extra estrogen and nothing to worry about.✦Some areas of your skin may darken.✦This is due to a temporary increase in pigment.✦If the darkening is on your lips, cheeks and forehead, it's called 'the mask of pregnancy' (melasma).✦You may also notice darkening on your nipples, dimples and scars, arms and vulva.✦The dark line running from your belly button down is known as the 'linea nigra'.✦These darker areas fade after birth.
134: ✦At this stage you may get leg cramps when lying down.✦In some cases they're caused by a lack of certain minerals.✦Increasing your calcium intake can ease cramps.✦Salt your food to taste, but avoid too much salt.✦It can raise blood pressure.✦Cramps can also happen if you don't drink enough or sit too much.
135: ✦By the end of this week you're expected to have gained about 5–6 kg on average.✦If your appetite has grown, it's time to slow down.✦Otherwise you may end pregnancy with excess weight.✦Excess weight isn't healthy and makes it harder for your body to recover and tone up after birth.
136: ✦If everything is fine, there's no harm in planning a holiday.✦A holiday is always good for couples, during pregnancy too.✦But keep a few things in mind when travelling: – Talk to your doctor before long trips. – When travelling by car, stop every 2 hours.✦During breaks, walk around or stretch your legs.
137: ✦Pay attention to your iron levels at this stage.✦You can get iron, important for your blood, from a balanced diet.✦Get checked regularly to reduce the risk of anaemia.✦Your iron levels may be affected by other things you consume.✦Calcium and the phenolic compounds in tea and coffee can reduce iron absorption.
138: ✦Before and during travel, avoid foods that upset your stomach.✦Don't overeat.✦Keep snacks like roasted chickpeas, dried fruit, raw hazelnuts, walnuts and almonds with you to balance your blood sugar and settle your stomach.
139: ✦On ultrasound your doctor checks your baby's physical development and the position of the placenta.✦You can hear your baby's heartbeat and see the hands and feet on the screen.✦But you may need your doctor's help to tell what's what.
140: ✦Your uterus has probably reached the level of your belly button.✦The curve in your lower back starts to flatten.✦Back pain may continue.✦Groin pain may continue and increase this week.✦These sharp pains, which can spread to the hips and belly, come from the uterus stretching the ligaments and muscles as it grows.
